info.title: underwrap admin API
info.description: Operator-facing JSON API exposed by `underwrap-backend` under `/v1/admin/*`. Authentication is session-cookie based (`__Host-underwrap-session`); state-changing requests must also carry the synchronizer CSRF header `X-CSRF-Token`. The mTLS runtime API is not part of this contract.

get.summary:
`GET /v1/admin/auth/bootstrap/status`. Returns setup-required only when the
sentinel is absent and the operator collection loads successfully as empty.
Every read or decode error fails closed to `false`.

200.description: True only when the operator collection is empty and the bootstrap-completed sentinel is unset.
Login succeeded; session cookie set.

500.description: Backend could not read user collection.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/admin/auth/password` — self-service password change for
the currently authenticated user. Requires the current password as
proof-of-possession.

200.description: Password changed; submitting-session refresh attempted.

400.description: Validation failed (e.g. new password too short).

500.description: Backend could not persist the change.

200.description: Returns the current operator, or an empty object if no session is present. Never 401 — designed for the SPA's bootstrap-redirect dance.
All client instances with action state and store mapping.
Client instance registered.
Instance updated. Cleanup of prior-store wrapper permissions after a remap is best effort; success does not certify their removal.
Instance removed. Cleanup of its mapped-store wrapper permissions is best effort; success does not certify their removal.
Fresh key generated without mutating storage; response carries exact no-cache headers.
Every store in the registry plus per-store usage projections.

post.description: Create a store. Encrypted creation requires `key_hex` as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters without trimming or normalization; plain creation requires it to be omitted. Explicit JSON `null` is invalid for every backend kind.

200.description: Store created and added to the registry.

400.description: Validation failed, including an explicit null `key_hex` (`invalid_request`) or conditional key errors (`key_required`, `unexpected_key`, or `invalid_key_hex`).

500.description: Backend could not persist the registry.

200.description: Store updated.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Optional; defaults to false. Pass `?force=true` to remove a nonempty or locked store record. Mapped runtime clients still block deletion; data directories are retained.

200.description: Store record removed; the data directory and retained generations are not deleted.

409.description: Store has mapped runtime clients (`store_in_use`), or force was omitted for a nonempty (`store_not_empty`) or locked (`store_locked_use_force`) store.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/admin/stores/{id}/lock` — drop the in-memory backend for
`name`, transitioning the registry to [`StoreState::Locked`]. The
held `MasterKey` zeroes on drop. Plain stores reject the
operation; already-locked stores succeed as a no-op so the admin
SPA can call this without racing the current state.

200.description: Store locked against new storage leases. Already admitted leases may retain the backend; its master key is zeroized when the final owner is dropped.

post.description: Migrate a store backend without changing its id. Migration to encrypted requires `key_hex` as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters without trimming or normalization; migration to plain requires it to be omitted. Explicit JSON `null` is invalid for every migration direction.

200.description: Store migrated at its stable id.

400.description: Request extraction or direction-specific key validation failed (`invalid_request`, `key_required`, `unexpected_key`, or `invalid_key_hex`).

409.description: Requested backend matches the current backend (`same_backend`).

200.description: Wrapper / resource pairs in the store.
Pair created.
Resource created and paired with the wrapper in one step.
Pair removed, or `ok: false` with structured blockers.
Resources in the store.
Resource created.
Resource renamed.
Resource deleted, or `ok: false` with structured blockers.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/admin/stores/{id}/rotate-key` — mint a fresh in-memory
master key, re-encrypt the complete store, atomically activate it, and
return the key once. Every displaced ciphertext generation remains in a
uniquely named backend-host recovery workspace until trusted manual cleanup.
HTTP delivery and the browser's local acknowledgement do not prove custody.

200.description: Key rotated and returned once; the displaced encrypted generation is retained for backend-host recovery.

parameters.name: resource_id
parameters.description: Restrict listing to a single resource.

200.description: Per-slot entries in the store (optionally filtered by resource id).

404.description: Store or filtered resource not found.

200.description: Secret entries and resources for the store, in one round trip.

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: Flat slot: env or files. Libsecret uses the structured resource endpoints.

200.description: Secret value, base64-encoded, or material_b64: null when the key is absent.

400.description: Invalid slot or key; libsecret is not a flat slot (`slot_not_supported`).

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: Flat slot: env or files. Libsecret uses the structured resource endpoints.

200.description: Secret written.

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: Flat slot: env or files. Libsecret uses the structured resource endpoints.

200.description: Secret removed; existed is false when the key was already absent.

400.description: Invalid slot or key; libsecret is not a flat slot (`slot_not_supported`).

post.summary:
Rename a per-slot entry inside a resource blob.
One load-modify-save removes the source key and inserts the destination in
the same in-memory pass; the storage layer then replaces the resource file
with one atomic rename. Concurrent whole-blob writers remain
last-writer-wins. Optionally overwrites material in the same step.

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: Flat slot: env or files. Libsecret uses the structured resource endpoints.

200.description: Secret renamed with atomic blob replacement; concurrent load-modify-save operations remain last-writer-wins.

400.description: Invalid slot, key, or material; libsecret is not a flat slot (`slot_not_supported`).

404.description: Store / resource / source key not found.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/admin/stores/{id}/unlock` — accept a 64-character hex
master key from the operator, build a fresh `EncryptedBackend`
against the store's data directory, verify the key by decrypting
the unlock canary written at creation, and install the backend in
the registry. Wrong keys never transition the registry to
`Unlocked`; the registry stays `Locked` and the response surfaces a
structured `key_mismatch` code.

200.description: Store unlocked.

400.description: Key hex is invalid (`invalid_key_hex`) or the store is not encrypted (`store_not_encrypted`).

403.description: Key does not match the encrypted store (`key_mismatch`).

500.description: Opening the store failed (`open_store_failed`), or trusted-host rotation or migration recovery is required (`rotation_recovery_required` or `migration_recovery_required`).

200.description: List of wrapper permissions for the store.
Permissions, pairs, and resources for the store, in one round trip.
Permission upserted.

404.description: Store, client instance, resource, or pair not found.

200.description: Permission removed.

Item created.

404.description: Store, resource, or collection not found.

200.description: Item removed (existed flag in body).

404.description: Store, resource, or collection not found.

200.description: Item secret material, base64-encoded.

404.description: Store, resource, collection, or item not found.

200.description: List of every operator in the collection.

500.description: Backend could not read the operator collection.

200.description: Operator created.

can_disable.description:
Whether this principal may transition the instance into the
disabled state.

can_enable.description:
Whether this principal may transition the instance back to the
active state.

auto_create_wrapper_assets.description:
Initial value for `auto_create_wrapper_assets`. Defaults to
`false` when omitted.

Whether this instance is allowed to auto-create resource and
wrapper/resource-pair records when its wrappers register on
startup. Defaults to `false` for newly-created instances.

New value for `auto_create_wrapper_assets`. Omit to leave
unchanged.

cert_pem.description:
Optional replacement client cert PEM. When set, the backend
parses it, validates it as a fresh client cert, replaces
`current_credential`, and updates the stored fingerprint.

AdminLibsecretAliasUpsertRequest.description:
`PUT .../libsecret/aliases/{name}`. `collection_id` must name an
existing collection; the handler returns 404 otherwise.

AdminLibsecretCollectionCreateRequest.description:
`POST .../libsecret/collections`. `id` is optional; when absent the
server derives one from the label.

AdminLibsecretCollectionDeleteResponse.description:
`DELETE .../libsecret/collections/{cid}`. The deletion cascades to
the collection's items in one save. Any aliases pointing at the
deleted collection are scrubbed atomically and their names
reported in `aliases_scrubbed`.

AdminLibsecretItemCreateRequest.description:
`POST .../libsecret/collections/{cid}/items`. `id` is optional; when
absent the server derives one from the label.

AdminLibsecretTreeResponse.description:
Whole-tree view of one resource's libsecret section. The shape
the admin SPA renders top-level.

aliases.description:
Alias name → collection id. Free-form name space at the
Service level; aliases pointing at non-existent collections
are not produced by this endpoint (the alias-PUT handler
enforces target existence).

collections.description:
Collections in id order. Item secret bytes are omitted; the
SPA fetches them on demand via the reveal endpoint.

AdminPairWithNewResourceRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/admin/stores/{id}/pairs/with-new-resource` —
create a fresh resource and pair it with `wrapper` in one request.
The resource catalogue and pair document are saved separately.
A failed pair save triggers best-effort resource rollback; the operation is
not transactional, and failed rollback can leave an unpaired resource.

AdminPasswordChangeRequest.description:
Self-service password change for the currently authenticated user.
Requires the current password as proof-of-possession of the
session. Distinct from `POST /v1/admin/users/{id}/password`, which
is the admin reset path and doesn't require the target's old
password.

AdminResourceDeleteBlockers.description:
Counts plus a short identifier-only sample per dependent kind. Samples are
capped server-side so a heavily-used resource does not return thousands of
entries. Identifiers are not copied into audit events or logs.

AdminResourceRenameRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /v1/admin/stores/{id}/resources/{rid}` — rename an
existing resource by id. The id stays stable; the name changes.

AdminSecretEntry.description:
One per-slot entry as listed by the admin surface. The flat-KV
admin endpoints (`env`, `files`) emit these; the `libsecret` slot
is structurally a tree and is addressed by its own endpoints, so
it never appears here.

AdminSecretRenameRequest.description:
Move an entry within a resource blob from the URL-addressed
`(resource_id, slot, from_key)` to `to_key` under the same slot,
optionally overwriting its material. The modified blob is persisted with
atomic replacement visibility, without an intermediate two-key state.
Loading, modifying, and saving are not a transaction: concurrent whole-blob
writers remain last-writer-wins.

`material_b64 = None` means "keep the existing material"; `Some(_)`
overwrites in the same replacement. A different existing destination is
rejected; renaming to the same key is permitted and can replace its material.

AdminStoreBackendKind.description:
Storage backend kind, independent of lifecycle state and action availability.
The admin API does not expose a separate store-detail endpoint or the
configured data directory in store list items.

AdminStoreCreateRequest.description:
Store creation request.

Encrypted creation requires `key_hex` to be exactly 64 lowercase
hexadecimal characters without trimming or normalization.
Plain creation requires `key_hex` to be omitted; explicit JSON `null` is
invalid for every backend kind.

key_hex.description:
Required exactly when `backend` is `encrypted`; otherwise omitted.
The accepted value is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

AdminStoreDeleteCleanupHint.description:
Structured hint for the manual cleanup the operator still has to
perform after a force-delete: the data dir was left in place so
the operator can decide whether to back it up, and the command
they would run to remove it.

id.description: Stable internal identifier used for routing and runtime mapping.

AdminStoreLockResponse.description:
Response of `POST /v1/admin/stores/{id}/lock`. Carries the
idempotence flag so the SPA can distinguish "we just locked the
store" from "store was already locked when we got here".

AdminStoreMigrateRequest.description:
Store backend migration request.

Migration to encrypted requires `key_hex` to be exactly 64 lowercase
hexadecimal characters without trimming or normalization.
Migration to plain requires `key_hex` to be omitted; explicit JSON `null`
is invalid for every migration direction.

key_hex.description:
Required exactly when `backend` is `encrypted`; otherwise omitted.
The accepted value is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

AdminStoreRotateKeyResponse.description:
Response from `POST /v1/admin/stores/{name}/rotate-key`. The new
key is returned exactly once. Every resource is re-encrypted before
the response is sent, while the displaced ciphertext generation remains
in a uniquely named backend-host recovery workspace until trusted manual
cleanup. `warning` explains that response delivery and local browser
acknowledgement do not prove external key custody. The backend never
persists the replacement key.

AdminStoreUnlockRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/admin/stores/{id}/unlock`. The operator pastes
in the 64-character hex master key that was issued at store
creation (or rotation). Whitespace around the value is tolerated.

description.description:
New description. Pass an empty string to clear it; omit to
leave it unchanged.

name.description:
New display name. Pass an empty string to clear it (invalid);
omit to leave it unchanged.

has_secrets.description:
Whether inspection found a non-control storage entry.
False also represents unavailable inspection for a locked, busy, or
recovery-required store; use lifecycle state and server-derived actions
rather than interpreting that value as proof of an empty store.

mapped_client_instance_count.description: How many runtime client instances currently map to this store.

password.description:
Plaintext on the wire (over TLS). Hashed server-side with
Argon2id before any storage step. Never echoed back.

AdminUserListItem.description:
One user record as visible to the admin UI. Mirrors
`crate::users::UserRecord` minus the password hash, which the API
never returns.

username.description: New username. Omit to keep the existing one.

AdminWrapperPermissionKey.description:
The composite key for a wrapper permission. Used in delete-refusal
responses so the SPA can render a "you must clear these wrapper
permissions first" list.

AdminWrapperPermissionUpsertRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /v1/admin/stores/{id}/wrapper-permissions/...`. The
`(client_instance, wrapper, resource_id)` tuple comes from the URL
path; the body holds the mutable parts of a `WrapperPermission`.

oneOf.description: An admin operator created this entity through the admin API.

id.description: The operator's stable id at creation time.

username.description:
The operator's username at creation time. Kept as a
denormalised copy so the field stays meaningful even if
the operator is later renamed or deleted.

oneOf.description:
A runtime client instance auto-created this entity via the
runtime register endpoint.

id.description: The instance's stable id at creation time.

EntityCreator.description:
Who created an entity record. Distinguishes admin operators (who
register resources/pairs by hand through the admin API) from
runtime client instances (which auto-create on startup when their
`auto_create_wrapper_assets` flag is on).

KvSecretSlot.description:
Subset of [`ResourceSlot`] that the flat-KV admin surface emits.
The `libsecret` slot is structurally a tree and is addressed by
its own admin endpoints, so it never appears in flat-entry listings.

ResourceRecord.description:
A resource record, one per store.

`id` is a stable, opaque, write-once identifier (`res_<hex>`). It
addresses the resource on disk (`resources/<id>` blob), in pair
records, and in wrapper permissions — so renaming a resource
preserves every existing reference.

`name` is the operator-facing label. Mutable via the admin rename
endpoint; what wrapper configs reference (operator-friendly); what
the SPA shows. Duplicates rejected on insert and on rename.

ServiceErrorResponse.description:
Generic structured error body returned by both the admin and runtime
surfaces. `code` is a stable machine token; `message` is human-facing.

ServiceWrapperResourcePair.description:
One `(wrapper, resource)` pair on the admin wire. Used in
resource-delete blocker payloads to name the dependent pairs that
would have to be cleaned up before the delete can proceed. The
persisted record (`WrapperResourcePairRecord`) adds provenance.

username.description:
Present when a session is attached; absent when the request is
unauthenticated. The SPA treats `username !== undefined` as
the authenticated check.

oneOf.description: Deny every invocation through this permission.
Allow real invocations; debug remains denied.

Allow invocations until `until_epoch`; deny afterwards. The expiry is
checked lazily on each request — no server-side sweeper.

Allow **both** the real wrapper and its debug variant until
`until_epoch`; deny afterwards. This is the only mode under which a
`variant = Debug` invocation is allowed — the debug tool can drop an
interactive shell or exec arbitrary commands with **read-write**
access to the projected secret (writebacks are accepted on the same
terms as `Real`, gated by `writable`), so it is gated behind an
explicit operator opt-in with a TTL. Expiry is checked lazily per
request.

WrapperPermission.description:
One per-store wrapper permission.

The tuple `(client_instance, wrapper, resource_id)` is the unique
key; persistence layers MUST reject duplicates with the stable
error code `duplicate_permission`. `resource_id` is the stable
backend id, so renaming a resource preserves every permission
that references it.

reason.description:
Operator-facing free-form note. Surfaced in the wrapper
permissions UI tooltip.

WrapperResourcePairRecord.description:
A `(wrapper, resource)` pair record, one per store.

`resource_id` references a [`ResourceRecord`] by its stable id;
the admin create endpoint refuses to create a pair whose resource
is not already present, and resource rename does not invalidate
the reference.

`last_used_at` is bumped server-side on every successful runtime
open and finalize against the pair. `None` means the pair has
never been used since the record was created.
